name: Alternate Picking
description: Strict down-up picking on a single string or simple pattern to build speed and evenness.

name: Downpicking
description: All downstrokes for a heavier, punchier attack, common in rock and metal rhythm parts.

name: String Skipping
description: Picking across non-adjacent strings cleanly without hitting the string in between.

name: Legato
description: Smooth hammer-on/pull-off runs with minimal picking, for fluid, singing lines.

name: Hammer-ons
description: Fretting-hand strikes that sound a note without picking, the building block of legato.

name: Pull-offs
description: The descending counterpart to hammer-ons; control and volume matching are the goal.

name: Bending
description: Pitch bends tuned by ear to a target interval (half step, whole step, and beyond).

name: Vibrato
description: Controlled pitch oscillation for expression; focus on consistent width and speed.

name: Slides
description: Sliding between frets while maintaining pressure and consistent tone.

name: Palm Muting
description: Muting strings with the picking-hand palm for a tighter, percussive sound.

name: Sweep Picking
description: One continuous picking motion across strings to outline arpeggios quickly.

name: Economy Picking
description: A hybrid of alternate and sweep picking that follows the most efficient path across strings.

name: Minor Pentatonic
description: The five-note scale behind most rock, blues, and pop guitar solos.

name: Major Pentatonic
description: The brighter major-key counterpart to the minor pentatonic.

name: Major Scale
description: The foundation scale for understanding keys, chords, and most Western music theory.

name: Natural Minor
description: The minor-key relative of the major scale, useful for minor-key soloing.

name: Blues Scale
description: The minor pentatonic plus a chromatic passing tone, central to blues phrasing.

name: Modes (Intro)
description: An introduction to the seven modes derived from the major scale.

name: Chord Changes
description: Switching cleanly between chord shapes without breaking tempo.

name: Strumming Patterns
description: Common down/up strumming patterns used across most songs.

name: Rhythm Accuracy
description: Playing exactly on the beat, verified against a metronome click.

name: Metronome Precision Drill
description: Deliberate practice locking single notes or strums to a click at varying tempos.

name: Fretboard Memorization
description: Naming notes anywhere on the neck from memory, without counting frets.

name: Note Identification
description: Recognizing notes by ear and by position, building toward sight-reading.

name: Interval Training
description: Recognizing and playing intervals (3rds, 5ths, and beyond) by ear and on the fretboard.
